clue.text: Create extra strain for a biologist

definitions.text: Create extra strain for a biologist

parts.note: surface reading: putting someone under more stress or pressure
setter's reading: a biologist makes a new strain, a hybrid, by pollinating one variety with another

explanation.surface: Someone piling additional stress on a scientist already working hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' reads as stress, but to a biologist it is a variety of plant or animal, and hybridising two of them makes a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hybridising between different varieties produces offspring forming a new breeding line, which is what a strain means in biology.

clue.text: Port served after all mem-bers had hefty snack

parts.note: a club is the whole body of members
Sandwich is a historic port in Kent, one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: After the port was handed round, the club members tucked into something substantial.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue writes 'Port served after' the members, so the port's name follows the word for all the members.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-layered sandwich with several fillings is a substantial bite between meals rather than a light one.

clue.text: More comfortable after pollarding willow

indicators.note: pollarding cuts the top off a tree, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more comfortable

explanation.surface: A tree is said to be happier once its branches have been lopped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the top is the first letter, so pollarding removes the C.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Someone getting browned off, still on the beach

definitions.text: Someone getting browned off, still on the beach

parts.words: Someone getting browned off, still on the beach
parts.note: surface reading: a fed-up person who has not yet left the shore, perhaps a marooned sailor
setter's reading: someone lying motionless on the sand being tanned

explanation.surface: A disgruntled person stuck on the beach, still waiting to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is British slang for fed up, and 'still' seems to mean 'yet'; read literally they mean tanned and lying motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lying in sunshine to acquire a tan is exactly someone being browned while keeping motionless.

clue.text: To conceal meaning of record, PC had to swap two letters

indicators.note: exchanging the positions of a pair of letters is a minimal rearrangement of what precedes

parts.note: an entry is an item recorded in a log or register
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hiding what a file says by having the computer jumble a couple of characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Joined, the two pieces nearly spell the answer; exchanging the T and the C finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Encoding a message turns it into cipher text so that outsiders cannot read what it says.

clue.text: In a class of my own, should I be true to form?

definitions.text: In a class of my own, should I be true to form?

parts.words: In a class of my own
parts.note: surface reading: someone peerless, unrivalled, wondering whether to behave as expected
setter's reading: a form is a school class, and the person in charge of their own class should be loyal to it

explanation.surface: A self-styled outstanding person wonders whether to act in their usual manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' and 'form' both sound like general words but are school groups, and the speaker is the one standing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmasters and schoolmistresses each run classes of pupils, often called forms in British schools.

clue.text: Clinging fabric sported by Darcy? Lizzie's taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being carried backwards, so the run of letters is read the other way
something sported is worn, so the letters are carried within the following words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of the first name and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Elizabeth Bennet is startled to see Mr Darcy in figure-hugging stretch material.
explanation.walkthrough: Darcy and Lizzie are the lovers of Pride and Prejudice; the answer runs backwards from inside Darcy into the L of Lizzie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trade name for a stretchy elastane fibre used in tight-fitting sportswear.

clue.text: Routine preparation — does it make you spit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dull groundwork done before the main task
second meaning: digging, where a spit is the depth of one blade's cut into the soil

explanation.surface: Wondering whether tedious groundwork is so annoying it makes one furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like rage or saliva, but a gardener's spit is one blade-depth of earth turned over in digging.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tedious preliminary effort, and literally means digging with a garden tool.

clue.text: Is one prepared to walk out for a wedding?

definitions.text: Is one prepared to walk out
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trade body whose members may go on strike
second meaning: a marriage, the joining of two people

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is ready to leave the church and head off to a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk out' sounds like a bride and groom leaving church, but here it means striking, which a labour organisation does.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage joins two people, and the word also names a body of workers organised to bargain collectively.

clue.text: First pairs chosen are coloured alike — dark grey

indicators.note: first pairs asks for the opening two letters of each following word

parts.note: opening two letters
opening two letters
opening two letters
opening two letters

explanation.surface: Teams picked first for a match turn out to be wearing the same strip.
explanation.walkthrough: This takes two letters from each word, not the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal names a very dark shade of grey, after the burnt wood used for drawing.

clue.text: Person showing crude quality, potentially brilliant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone unpolished in manner but good at heart
second meaning: an uncut gem that could become a sparkling brilliant once cut

explanation.surface: Someone with unrefined gifts who might yet turn out to be a star.
explanation.walkthrough: A brilliant is also a gem cut with many facets, which an uncut stone may become.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a good-hearted but unpolished person and literally an unworked gemstone.

clue.text: Run 20, getting hungry at last — like some bacon?

parts.note: 20 across is NAKED, and to run naked through a crowd is to streak

indicators.note: at last points to only the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: final letter only

explanation.surface: A runner who has covered twenty miles is ravenous and dreaming of a fry-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 20 refers to another answer in the grid, not a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky bacon is cut from the belly and has alternating layers of fat and lean.

clue.text: Stop travelling overseas

parts.note: surface reading: give up foreign trips
setter's reading: a ship travelling on the sea comes to a halt with its head to the wind

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit holidaying abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overseas' suggests abroad, but it means on the sea itself, where this nautical phrase is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing term means bringing a vessel to a standstill without anchoring, by setting sails against each other.

clue.text: Nick passage for piano Tchaikovsky used

indicators.note: a passage is an excerpt, so the letters are a short stretch lifted from the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone pinches a piece of piano music the great Russian composer once played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a verb meaning steal, but it is a noun: a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut in an edge, which is what a nick is.

clue.text: Be encouraged by sequence of film — earth-shattering!

parts.note: a take is one continuous filmed shot

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into fragments, so the preceding word's letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheered up by a stunning scene from a disaster movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth-shattering' reads as stunning, but splits into a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is an idiom meaning to gain courage or feel more hopeful.

clue.text: Air of unrequited love transformed mostly corny ghost

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word drops its final letter
transformed means changed in shape, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: corny without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentimental ghost story turned into a lovelorn ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch song is a sad ballad lamenting a lost or unreturned romance, as in carrying a torch for someone.

clue.text: Cope with pub that's used by bikers

parts.note: to handle something is to cope with it
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Putting up with a drinking place frequented by motorcycle gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: A biker bar is the picture, but bikers use the steering bar of a bicycle or motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclists and motorcyclists steer by gripping the bar fixed across the front fork.

clue.text: Come to steal from trendy lords and ladies?

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
to rob is to steal from
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Arriving to pick the pockets of fashionable aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' seems to be the nobility, but it is the country name of the wild arum plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wake-robin is another folk name for the cuckoo-pint, the woodland arum also called lords and ladies.

clue.text: Graduate's mum finally going off Tim Rice's style

definitions.note: the answer is a kind of rice, so 'style of rice'

indicators.note: the final letter going off means it is dropped from the end of the next word

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate, plus the S
ma is an informal word for mother
the name with its last letter gone

explanation.surface: A graduate's mother leaves while Tim Rice's lyric-writing style is discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice is the lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar, but here 'Rice' is the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a variety of long-grain rice grown in India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Gets in information about object of savings policy

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the combined letters are read the other way
in places the first word inside the following one

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone learns about the purpose of an investment plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sits inside the slang word after its first letter, and 'about' then turns the whole thing round; 'Gets in' looks like a phrasal verb but is word plus container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum put aside for the future, the goal of a savings plan.

clue.text: Wearing suit received for birthday

parts.note: surface reading: dressed in a new suit given as a present
setter's reading: the suit one is born in is bare skin

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed up in a smart suit they were given as a birthday present.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing your 'birthday suit' is a jokey idiom for having no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in your birthday suit means being unclothed, as on the day you were born.

clue.text: In which one conspires about Scots, showing irritation

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
hoots is a Scots exclamation of impatience or irritation

explanation.surface: Someone plotting over Scottish affairs gets visibly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The irritation belongs to the Scots, whose cry of 'hoots!' expresses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in secret partnership, the state where conspirators plot together.

clue.text: Approval given, without a hint of hesitation, for stopgap material

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word goes round the single letter

parts.note: OK signals approval
taken as written
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Something is approved without the slightest pause as a temporary fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside, not lacking, so the A sits inside OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose tarred fibre packed into ships' seams to stop the gaps, so it is literally gap-stopping stuff.

clue.text: "Lassie" translated to accommodate one part of Europe

indicators.note: translated means converted into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The famous collie's film is dubbed to suit a foreign market.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the collie of the films and TV series; 'accommodate' just takes in the extra letter before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, now mostly in Poland.

clue.text: This situation starts to seem naughty and frankly untoward

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A messy state of affairs is beginning to look rude and rather improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is military slang for a chaotic mess, politely 'situation normal, all fouled up', which fits 'naughty' and 'untoward'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a confused, botched state of affairs, so it names a muddled situation.

clue.text: Dismiss ethnic origin in sports day event

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
race is ethnic origin

explanation.surface: Firing someone because of their background at a school games day.
explanation.walkthrough: Sports day is the British school athletics afternoon, where children race with their legs in bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping along in sacks is a classic novelty contest at school athletics afternoons.

clue.text: Support leads to 50% of vote — well done!

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: its first half

explanation.surface: Backing helps a candidate to half the ballot, earning congratulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of praise or applause for a fine performance.

clue.text: Behave like Rumpelstiltskin, maybe, where one's haunted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the fairy tale he stamps his foot into the earth in rage
second meaning: a favourite haunt, the place one frequents

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale imp in a fury, and a place visited by ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunted' suggests ghosts, but one's haunt is simply where one regularly goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's stamping ground is the area they habitually frequent, their usual haunt.
